_comment: SEEDED by `wowkb.capart import scenarios` from specs/havoc/scenarios.md, then reviewed by eye. The DOC leads: `capart check` re-scrapes the CDM-row bullets and fails if they disagree with this file. Edit the doc, re-import, review.

scenarios.title: Metamorphosis — the reset is banked
scenarios.state: Not transformed, Fury ~50. Vengeful Retreat and Metamorphosis are up; Eye Beam and Blade Dance are both on cooldown. The Hunt is up. Nothing is in a window.

steps.html: Vengeful Retreat — off the GCD; weave it now, for free (holds Exergy). Continue for the GCD press.

Metamorphosis — available, and it carries two dependency dots, shown only while it is castable: Eye Beam and Death Sweep, each driven by that ability's readable cooldown state. go = on cooldown (the reset is valuable); wait = ready (the reset would be wasted). Both read go here → the reset banks two casts → press.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: Meta's own readiness didn't decide it — the state of the two abilities it resets did. Two dots are richer than one hold marker: they say why it is go, and they say it from readable facts.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readiness (R2) → have. Reset dots — Eye Beam & Death Sweep cooldowns (R7, readable) → have.

scenarios.title: Eye Beam — Metamorphosis waits (the counter)
scenarios.state: Same as ST-1, but **Eye Beam is *ready*** (Blade Dance still on cooldown). Meta is up.

steps.html: Vengeful Retreat — weave, off-GCD.
Metamorphosis — available, but its Eye Beam dot flips to wait: Eye Beam is ready, so resetting it would waste the reset. Meta reads hold-readable → skip.
The Hunt — on cooldown → skip.
Eye Beam — available, no skip-reason → press. Cast it now; Meta resets it a moment later for a banked second cast.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: The mirror of ST-1, and the strongest demonstration: cap re-ranks the press from a readable relationship between two buttons, computing nothing.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readiness (R2) → have. Reset dot — Eye Beam cooldown (R7, readable) → have.

scenarios.title: The Hunt — Metamorphosis is down
scenarios.state: Not transformed. The Hunt is up; Metamorphosis is on cooldown. Eye Beam on cooldown. Fury mid.

steps.html: Vengeful Retreat — weave, off-GCD.
Metamorphosis — on cooldown → skip.
The Hunt — available; its one dependency dot reads Meta's cooldown state. Meta is on cooldown → dot reads go → there is no upcoming Meta to sync with, so cast now → press.

extras.label: Counter
extras.html: If Metamorphosis were up, The Hunt's dot flips to wait — hold, to save The Hunt to buff Abyssal Gaze inside the coming Meta window (the guide's "hold if Metamorphosis is available"). You would skip The Hunt and press the next GCD button.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readiness (R2) → have. Sync-hold dot — Meta cooldown state (R7, readable) → have. (Corrects an earlier draft that made this a sealed Essence-Break-window hold — the live guide's hold is Meta-availability, which cap reads directly.)

scenarios.title: Death Sweep — flood the window (demon-form override)
scenarios.state: Transformed — Metamorphosis is active. You have just opened an Essence Break window with Fury banked. Eye Beam (→ Abyssal Gaze) and Essence Break are on cooldown.

steps.html: Vengeful Retreat — weave, off-GCD.
Metamorphosis / The Hunt / Abyssal Gaze / Essence Break — all on cooldown (spent to build and open the window) → skip.
Death Sweep — available, and the readable demon-form window promotes it above what a lit COOLDOWN would be (promoted > lit COOLDOWN) → press. Flood the window.

extras.label: Fidelity
extras.html: This is the override showcase: the row now reads Abyssal Gaze · Death Sweep · Annihilation · Consuming Fire. cap authors none of it — R7 resolves the live overrideSpellID, so the CDM shows precisely what the client shows.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Demon-form promotion (D, R7) → have. Demonsurge-active promotion → open. Essence-Break-window promotion → open. (Demon form carries the promotion today; the two windows would sharpen it if their active-state proves readable — until then they mark, never promote.)

scenarios.title: Essence Break — open the window (sealed cues)
scenarios.state: Not transformed, Fury banked (≥35), no window live. Essence Break is up. Eye Beam's cooldown has more than 4s remaining (safe to open).

steps.html: Vengeful Retreat — weave, off-GCD.
Metamorphosis / The Hunt — on cooldown → skip.
Eye Beam — on cooldown, long remaining → skip.

Essence Break — available, and it carries the banked cue: the client evaluated secret Fury against an authored break point (35 / maxFury, S1) and painted it — cap never read the value → press, then flood the ~4s window with Death Sweep + Annihilation. ⚠ The banked cue is open (below), so it produces nothing until measured; the artifact marks it as such.

extras.label: Counter
extras.html: If Eye Beam's cooldown had ≤4s remaining instead, Essence Break would read hold-sealed — don't clip the window into Eye Beam. That hold rides a sealed duration (S4 curve on Eye Beam's cooldown), painted client-side; cap never reads the clock. You would skip Essence Break, spend the baseline spender, and open the window after Eye Beam.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readiness (R2) → have. Banked-Fury ≥35 threshold (S1 positive, painted) → open (the positive-polarity threshold cue is specified but unmeasured; until confirmed the press ships on readiness + player judgment, no banked light). Sealed hold — Eye Beam CD ≤4s (C2, S4) → sealed.

scenarios.title: Death Sweep / Blade Dance — the baseline spender
scenarios.state: Not transformed, Fury mid (affordable). Every cooldown above is on cooldown. Immolation Aura is not full.

steps.html: Vengeful Retreat … Essence Break — all on cooldown → skip.
Blade Dance — available and affordable → press. The ordinary spender; it wins by elimination — nothing above it is up, and it needs no cue of its own.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: The canonical elimination case for the middle of the list. Whenever a cooldown returns, the field re-lights above it and the eye moves up — which is exactly the priority order.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readiness (R2) → have. Affordability (A) → have (dims if Fury-starved — see ST-7).

scenarios.title: Felblade — Fury-starved (affordability, with overcap counter)
scenarios.state: Not transformed, Fury low, no cooldown up, Immolation not full.

steps.html: Vengeful Retreat … Essence Break — on cooldown → skip.
Blade Dance — available but reads starved: you cannot afford it (cue A, the insufficientPower read) → skip.
Chaos Strike — same, starved → skip.
Immolation Aura — available, but its charges read below full → secret, so cap withholds the "spend it" opinion (unknown ≠ capped) → skip, no signal.

Felblade — a generator with no Fury cost, so it is never unaffordable; it keeps its emphasis while the spenders lose theirs → press. Rebuild Fury; the generator correctly rises past the starved spenders because the field around it fell away.

extras.label: Counter
extras.html: With Fury near cap instead, the same Felblade reads overcap (cue B, negative) — pressing it would waste Fury. You skip the generator and spend a spender. The break point is authored (S1); the client paints it; cap reads nothing.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readiness (R2) → have. Affordability (A) → have. Immolation withhold (R6) → have. Overcap readout (B, S1 negative) → sealed.

scenarios.title: Immolation Aura — don't cap the charges
scenarios.state: Not transformed, Immolation Aura at full (2/2 with A Fire Inside). The spenders are on cooldown (just spent). Fury mid.

steps.html: Everything above, including both spenders, is on cooldown → skip.

Immolation Aura — its charges read full (R6: the charge count reads plain only at max), so cap emphasises it as "spend it" → press. Don't waste a charge; dump both before Meta so A Fire Inside / Demonic Intensity refunds them.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: Below full the count is secret and the button reads withheld — the plain full read is the whole capped signal. This is the one Fury-adjacent decision that matters, and R6's read-at-full limit is a feature here, not a hole.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Immolation-at-full (R6) → have (open-to-confirm: does the charge row read readable-at-full in instanced combat? confirm before shipping the tier).

scenarios.title: Annihilation / Chaos Strike — the raw dump (elimination, low)
scenarios.state: Not transformed, Fury flush, no window live. Blade Dance is on cooldown; Immolation not full.

steps.html: Everything above, and Blade Dance, is on cooldown → skip.

Chaos Strike — available and affordable (Fury flush) → press. The raw dump lives near the bottom of the list; it is the press only by elimination — it is the only emphasised spender — and cap gives it no more than its baseline lane treatment. It wins by being alone.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: The reason cap must not over-emphasise the bottom: the raw dump stands out only relative to a quieter field. The generators to its right read overcap (Fury is flush), so the eye is pushed toward spending, not generating. Were Fury low, Chaos Strike would read starved (cue A) and a generator would rise past it (ST-7).

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readiness (R2) → have. Affordability (A) → have. Overcap readout on the generators (B) → sealed.

scenarios.title: Fel Rush — last-resort filler
scenarios.state: Not transformed. Both spenders were just spent and are on cooldown, Immolation Aura is not full, and Fury is flush — so both generators would waste it.

steps.html: Every cooldown and both spenders are on cooldown; Immolation Aura is withheld; both generators read overcap → skip → Fel Rush is all that is left → press. The fallback has no signal of its own; the eye lands here purely by elimination. (An earlier draft wrote this row as an ellipsis — "every rotation button cd / starved" — which no state actually produces: a generator has no Fury cost and so can never be starved. The row above is the state that genuinely reaches the filler.)

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readiness (R2) → have. (Throw Glaive is not in the Fel-Scarred priority — a rare filler unless Screaming Brutality routes it through Blade Dance; with Serrated Glaive it buffs you* for 12s, a candidate buff-maintenance marker, open.) --- ## AoE / cleave variants (3+ targets) The AoE list shares the same row and only re-weights the middle — the single-target raw spender drops, and Immolation Aura + Blade Dance/Death Sweep rise. It adds no new cues. The re-weight is selected by the player's AoE-mode input (../spec.md §2 — the player sets single-target or AoE), not* by a readable target count (cap has no readable enemy count and would not compute one). So these are the ST scenarios above with the mode input shifting which button the walk reaches first.

extras.label: Delta
extras.html: In AoE mode Immolation Aura is a top source, pressed harder than the single "don't cap at 2" rule. cap's cue is unchanged — the readable-at-full "don't cap" signal (R6) still fires; the press-it-more is the AoE-mode input, not a new cue and not a computed count.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Immolation-at-full (R6) → have. AoE-mode weighting → mode input, not a cue.

extras.label: Delta
extras.html: In AoE mode these rise to primary (they trigger Glaive Tempest at 3+). The rise is the AoE-mode input; the demon-form promotion (D) still stacks on top when transformed, and the single-target Chaos Strike dump falls beneath it.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readiness (R2) → have. Demon-form promotion (D) → have. AoE-mode weighting → mode input, not a cue.

extras.label: Delta
extras.html: In AoE mode the single-target dump drops further beneath Blade Dance — spend into Blade Dance instead. The AoE-mode input re-ranks an already-by-elimination button (ST-9) below the generators; the re-rank is the narrowing, no new cue.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readiness (R2) → have. Affordability (A) → have. AoE-mode weighting → mode input, not a cue. (Still reached only by elimination, just lower.) (Burning-Wound tab-targeting and the Meta + Essence Break AoE burst add no cap cue: tab-targeting is target selection cap does not hint, and the Meta/EB burst is the same COOLDOWN readiness as ST.) --- ## What the walk surfaced — cue completeness + gaps Complete cue set for comprehensive coverage (have / sealed): readiness (R2), affordability (A), readable hold / dependency dots C1 (incl. the reset dots and the sync-hold dot), sealed hold C2, demon-form promotion (D), Immolation-at-full (R6), overcap readout (B negative), banked-Fury threshold (S1 positive), identity re-skin (R7), and the demon-form bar. Plus two non-cue mechanisms the walk made explicit: the emphasis-intensity hierarchy and eye-direction by elimination (both now ../spec.md §3.1), and the AoE-mode input that re-weights without a readable count. Route every one as @verify-ingame / ClientLab @pending-test, never a guess. None gates a press — each only sharpens a scenario that already resolves by a readable cue or elimination.
